features.title: What db-ops can do
features.sub: Your agent becomes a data-ops assistant the moment it is installed.

items.d: SELECT queries and schema inspection out of the box — PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite.
UPDATE / DELETE / DROP show a plan block first, then require a typed confirmation like confirm-DELETE-LOCAL-4. No accidental deletions.
Wrap multi-step workflows (invite codes, weekly reports…) into one trigger phrase.
Any database you can reach: localhost, a VPS, or cloud DBs — RDS, Railway, Neon, Supabase and more.
Every operation is logged with connection, type and row counts. Ask "what happened today?" anytime.
Add recipes, query logs, confirm dangerous operations — all inside the conversation.
Chat in Chinese and it replies in Chinese; chat in English and it replies in English.
Connections are whitelist-only, chmod 600, gitignored, and never shown in full.

recipes.title: Community recipes
recipes.sub: Ready-to-use workflows contributed by the community — copied with one click, imported with one paste.
recipes.what: Recipes turn frequent multi-step operations — generating an invite code, running a weekly report — into a single trigger phrase. Instead of repeating a 5-step manual workflow, you say one sentence and db-ops drafts, confirms and executes the whole flow. They live in .dbops/recipes.json (project-level) or ~/.dbops/recipes.json (global).
recipes.how1: Copy the JSON of a recipe you like — from the cards below or the Gallery page.
recipes.how2: Paste it into your agent chat and say "add this recipe" — preview it, confirm, done.
recipes.how3: When asked, bind the recipe's connection to one of your whitelisted connections (shared recipes use the YOUR_DB placeholder).
recipes.howNote: You can also edit .dbops/recipes.json by hand — each entry is plain JSON.
recipes.empty: No recipes yet — be the first to share one!

faqs.title: FAQ
faqs.sub: Common questions about using db-ops in real scenarios.

items.a: Install the skill (one line above), restart your agent session, then create a .dbops/.env file in your project with one connection string per line. That's it — just tell the agent what you need, e.g. "show me the users table structure".

items.q: Where are my connection strings stored? Is it safe?
items.a: In .dbops/.env (project) or ~/.dbops/.env (global). The file is chmod 600 and gitignored; the skill only connects to connections listed there (whitelist) and never prints passwords — you always see postgres://user:***@host.

items.q: Can the AI accidentally delete my data?
items.a: Dangerous operations (UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / TRUNCATE / ALTER) show a plan block with a row count first, then require a typed confirmation string like confirm-DELETE-LOCAL-4 that you must type exactly — "yes / Y" are never accepted. DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE is treated as a mistake and needs your explicit confirmation.
PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite — locally, on a VPS, or in the cloud (AWS RDS, Railway, Neon, Supabase, Tencent/Aliyun RDS…). The type is auto-detected from the connection string.
No problem — the skill falls back to a temporary postgres:16 Docker container that is discarded after use. Connection strings are never written to disk.

items.q: What are recipes and how do I add them?
items.a: Recipes turn multi-step workflows into one trigger phrase. Add one right in the chat: "add a recipe that generates invite codes" — the agent drafts it, you approve, it is saved and validated. Manual editing of recipes.json works too.

items.q: How do I check the audit logs?
items.a: Just ask: "show me today's log" or "which dangerous operations happened". Logs live in .dbops/logs/<date>.log and are read-only for the skill. Passwords never appear in them.
Yes — db-ops adapts to the language of your conversation. Chat in Chinese and everything (plans, confirmations, receipts) comes back in Chinese; chat in English and it replies in English.

items.q: Can I use it with Cursor / Zed / other tools?
items.a: Yes — anything that supports SKILL.md. Copy the db-ops folder into the tool's skills directory (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/) and restart your session.

items.q: How can I share a recipe with the community?
items.a: Open a recipe issue via the issue form — once approved, it is automatically added to the gallery. You can also paste recipe JSON into any chat and say "add this recipe".
